q: A work order is produced before the Workshop Accounts Office on which the head of account to which the cost of the job is chargeable is not indicated. The correct position is that:

options.A: Every work order must invariably indicate the allocation, and expenditure on the job is booked to the head so indicated
options.B: The allocation may be decided by the shop incharge at the time of completion of the job
options.C: The cost of such a job is booked to shop on-cost until an allocation is allotted
options.D: The allocation is required only on work orders for jobs done for other railways

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Time keeping in a workshop refers to recording the attendance of workers, that is, their time of arrival at and departure from the workshop.
2. Time booking in a workshop refers to recording the time spent by a worker on each job on which he is engaged.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Material drawn for a workshop job is returned to the stores depot as surplus after completion of the job. The job is credited for the returned material:

options.A: At the current market price on the date of return
options.B: At the same price at which the material was issued to the job
options.C: At half of its issue price, the balance being charged to on-cost
options.D: At a price fixed by the shop incharge at the time of return

q: A job in progress in a workshop is abandoned midway and is not to be completed. The expenditure already accumulated on it under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is:

options.A: Carried forward unchanged from year to year without any orders
options.B: Recovered from the wages of the workers who were engaged on the job
options.C: Automatically transferred to the Pension Fund
options.D: Adjusted under the orders of the competent authority, and is not allowed to remain indefinitely under the suspense head

q: During the clearance of a shop, scrap is found lying there which cannot be linked to any particular job. The value of such scrap is accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting its value to shop on-cost
options.B: Crediting its value to the last job completed in the shop
options.C: Debiting its value to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.D: Crediting its value to the first job taken up in the following month

q: In the Balance Sheet of a railway, the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is reflected as:

options.A: A liability of the railway towards the workshop staff
options.B: A revenue receipt of the year in which the jobs were taken up
options.C: An asset, representing the work-in-progress in the workshops
options.D: A part of the Pension Fund of the railway

q: The connecting link between the cost accounts of a workshop and its financial (Government) accounts is:

options.A: The priced stores ledger maintained in the stores depot
options.B: The Workshop Manufacturing Suspense head in the financial books and the Workshop General Register in the cost books
options.C: The Traffic Book of the railway
options.D: The contractor's ledger maintained for works contracts

q: On the accounts side, the Workshop Accounts Officer of a railway workshop functions under:

options.A: The Chief Workshop Manager of the workshop
options.B: The Controller of Stores of the zonal railway
options.C: The Railway Audit office of the zone
options.D: The Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer of the zonal railway

q: The Account Current rendered by the accounts office of a workshop is:

options.A: A statement of the cash balance held in the workshop imprest
options.B: A list of the jobs remaining incomplete at the end of the year
options.C: A periodical (monthly) statement of the transfer transactions between the workshop accounting unit and other accounting units
options.D: A statement of the stores issued to jobs during the day

q: An estimate prepared for a manufacture job in a railway workshop provides for:

options.A: Labour, material and on-cost required for the job
options.B: Material cost of the job only
options.C: Labour cost of the job only
options.D: On-cost of the job only

q: Associated finance vetting of a manufacture estimate of a railway workshop, before it is sanctioned by the competent authority, is carried out by:

options.A: The Production Control Organisation alone
options.B: The Workshop Accounts Office
options.C: The stores depot attached to the workshop
options.D: The Railway Board in all cases

q: Articles manufactured under a batch work order are completed and ready in lots before the entire batch is finished. The cost of such articles is transferred out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense:

options.A: Only after the last article of the batch is completed
options.B: At the end of the financial year, for the whole batch together
options.C: Only after the batch work order is formally closed by the Railway Board
options.D: Lot-wise, as and when each lot is completed and transferred to stores

q: Castings for several jobs are poured from a common melt in the foundry of a workshop. The common melting cost is apportioned among the jobs on the basis of:

options.A: The weight of metal poured for each job
options.B: The number of workers engaged in the foundry
options.C: The floor area occupied by the foundry
options.D: The number of moulding boxes used for the melt

q: The cost of service shops of a workshop, such as the tool room and the power house, is brought into the cost of jobs by:

options.A: Charging it directly to the first job taken up in the year
options.B: First apportioning it among the production shops served, whose on-cost is then absorbed on their jobs
options.C: Debiting it to Stores Suspense until the close of the year
options.D: Writing it off to revenue at the end of the year

q: Before it is distributed over the jobs of a shop, the shop on-cost of the shop is first collected:

options.A: Directly in the Balance Sheet of the railway
options.B: In the Stores Suspense account of the depot
options.C: Under separate on-cost (standing) work orders maintained for the shop
options.D: Through the contractor's ledger of the workshop

q: Jobs executed by a workshop for its own railway are transferred out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense on the principle that the workshop works on a no-profit-no-loss basis, that is, the outturn is transferred at:

options.A: The market price of the article or work
options.B: Cost plus a fixed percentage of profit
options.C: The purchase price of a similar article in the market
options.D: The cost of production
